correctness.rationale: For crown graph C_n=K_(n,n) minus its diagonal perfect matching, edge-uniform greedy matching at m remaining pairs with r intact forbidden pairs has m²-r legal edges. Counts of transitions r→r,r-1,r-2 are (m-r)²,2r(m-r),r(r-1), and at m=1 failure iff r=1. The normalized first moment telescopes to 2/(n+1)-p_n = 4∑ E[R_m(R_m-1)/(m(m-1)(m+1)(m²-R_m))]. Tagged two-label survival probabilities yield uniform E(R_m)_2 = [m(m-1)]²/[n(n-1)] (1+O(1/m)); substituting proves 4 log n/[n(n-1)]+O(n^-2). Independently exact-rational DP confirmed p2=0, p3=1/3, p4=p5=4/21 and further values through n=12. This is mathematically correct but scientifically covered.

evidence: Uniform logarithmic correction theorem states for ALL 0<=r<=n a uniform finite inequality |p_(n,r)-(2r/(n(n+1))-4v_(n,r)(H_n-1))|<=36v_(n,r).
Setting r=n yields v=1/[(n+1)(n+2)] and the identical crown rare-failure logarithmic correction plus an O(n^-2) uniform remainder.

originality.rationale: FAIL: Complete previously published Resultary theorem Uniform logarithmic correction for greedy matching with partially forbidden pairs treats precisely this same uniform-feasible-edge process on K_(n,n) with any r disjoint forbidden edges. Its sharp bound |p_(n,r)-[2r/(n(n+1))-4v_(n,r)(H_n-1)]|<=36v_(n,r), v_(n,r)=r(r-1)/[n(n-1)(n+1)(n+2)], applies at r=n, giving v=1/[(n+1)(n+2)] and p_n=2/(n+1)-4 log n/[n(n-1)]+O(n^-2); it includes the same two-parameter recurrence. This is a stronger domination for every r, not just a title match. The 2026-11-02 crown theorem also already gave the same exact recurrence and first-order 2/n law. The strictly stronger result has the same Nov 8 publication date as the submitted package, so exact within-day priority cannot be claimed; existing mathematical coverage is decisive for acceptance.
residual_risks: The general r theorem and the submitted finding both carry 2026-11-08 publication dates; intra-day priority is unestablished, but mathematical coverage is unambiguous.
Full 1991 Dyer–Frieze historical article was inaccessible; this is not needed for the decisive coverage rejection.
